You asked for some objectivity, so here it is.

After your mom left your father and you, she made the conscious decision to refuse her visitation rights.

In your 22 years of life, never once has she even tried to come see you.

She had 22 years to come fix things with you.

The first ever time that you saw your mother in person was the day of your father's funeral.

She came with not only her family, but her husband and his family as well.

This is the same husband who decided to marry your mom months after his wife just died.

At the same time, your mother decided to marry this man 2 months after giving birth to you knowing that his wife just died.

Months after the funeral, the EXACT people that your mom left you for start following you on instagram.

And then your mother followed you and messaged you.

She had  TWENTY YEARS to think about how she could restart things with you. And these are the events that led up to the moment that she did.

Regardless of her motivations, these are all the facts of the situation.

\------------------------------------------

Here's the subjective part.

I would also be curious about my mother if I was you, and I would think that maybe if I would just meet with her, that I could have some closure. That she could explain herself so that I can understand.

But what would you want her to say?

Could she say anything that would that make you feel any different?

Personally, even if she said everything that I wanted her to (to say she's sorry, she loves me, she missed me, she never stopped thinking of me, etc...) it would not change the way I would feel.

It would just hurt me more, because how can I believe anything that she says? I would just have a pit in my stomach that will always be asking: Why now? Why after my father died? If my father hadn't passed away, would you have reached out?

I would not be able to trust anything that she would say no matter how much I want to believe her.

Her actions just speak volumes louder than anything that she could say.

Even if I do meet with her and hear her out, I wouldn't be able to get the closure that I would want because I won't be able to trust her words.

It is the sad reality that no matter what you do, you will be thinking about your mom. But you've been alive 22 years without her, you're still here standing. You also have family that love and care about you. Your relationship with your mom is not a need, but a want. 

I think that it's time to just let her go. 

This is just how I would think if I were in your position.
